content: Apologies if this is a naive question, but is Chaitin's incompleteness theorem something that could eventually be proved in Lean? It seems to require a sort of meta-proving ability that Lean doesn't have right now.
it looks like it's saying something about the strength of formal systems
you would have to formalize formal systems and formalize the statement of complexity within those formal systems within Lean
yeah, it might be something for the FormalizedFormalLogic project to tackle

creating a method of generating all valid proofs and then extracting the description of the string under analysis from a given proof might be tricky

though maybe the existence of the enumerator and extraction methods could be an assumption

So I asked Aristotle to come up with something and it wasn't half bad

it defined Kolmogorov Complexity this way:

/-- Kolmogorov complexity: the minimum encoding of a code that outputs `n` on input 0. -/
noncomputable def K (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf { Encodable.encode c | c ∈ {c : Code | n ∈ c.eval 0} }

and here's how it defined Chaitin's incompleteness theorem:

/-- **Chaitin's Incompleteness Theorem.**

A formal system is modeled as a code `e` that enumerates pairs `⟨s, L⟩`
(using `Nat.pair`), representing claims "`K(s) > L`".

If the system is *sound* — every claim it makes is true — then there
exists a bound `B` such that the system never claims `K(s) > L` for
any `L > B`.

In other words, no sound computably enumerable formal system can prove
lower bounds on Kolmogorov complexity beyond a fixed threshold determined
by the system's own complexity. -/
theorem chaitin_incompleteness (e : Code)
    (sound : ∀ k m, m ∈ e.eval k → K (Nat.unpair m).1 > (Nat.unpair m).2) :
    ∃ B, ∀ k m, m ∈ e.eval k → (Nat.unpair m).2 ≤ B
and then it proved everything (weirdly there were a couple exact? statements left that I had to manually apply, but after I did so I didn't see any issues)
the choice to model the formal system as a Code is a bit weird, but I was impressed that it came up with anything at all

This is a toy model from Aristotle. Just a heads-up: Kolmogorov complexity isn't in Mathlib yet, but I've already formalized the foundational theory here: https://github.com/AlexeyMilovanov/kolmogorov-complexity-lean

I'm currently in the process of upstreaming these basics to Mathlib.Computability. Would be great to formalize Chaitin's theorem once the core AIT infrastructure is merged.

Just a quick update on this: I've actually just finished formalizing Chaitin's Incompleteness Theorem in the repository. Independence is shown for any axiomatic system in which co-enumerable sets can be expressed and the set of provable statements is enumerable.

The FormalizedFormalLogic/Foundation repository actually has the necessary machinery to show that Peano Arithmetic satisfies these exact properties. Unfortunately, their repository does not work on the modern Lean.
